journey.name: TL-09 A second delete replaces the first undo offer
journey.description:
KNOWN-DEFECT WATCHLIST. Expected to fail if the current behaviour is judged wrong; see qa/TEST-PLAN.md.
TaskListUiState holds a single nullable message, so a second delete overwrites the first TaskDeleted before the user can act on it. The first task is then unrecoverable - undo is the only route back, it is offered once, and the offer is gone.
This journey asserts the behaviour as it stands. Deciding whether a queue, a longer window or an accepted limitation is right is a product call, not a QA one; what the suite owes is that the limitation is visible rather than discovered by a user.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Renew domain registration" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Immediately tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Reply to design feedback" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "Reply to design feedback" is on screen again
Verify that "Renew domain registration" is not on screen and is offered no further way back
